messages:
maria: Heads up — after the collector change yesterday we're seeing a steady climb in telemetry-ingest CPU p99 and exporter queueing. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/telemetry/ingest?panel=cpu :eyes:

josh: saw that. p50 ok, p99 jumps around 750ms -> 1.4s on the exporter handoff. Any new attr processors landed?

maria: yep, the attr_normalizer was moved into the post-batch hotpath to de-dup string keys. suspected perf win but looks like it increased per-span work and delayed batching windows.

vikram: moving a heavy processor after batching will serialise the pipeline. It can extend batch processing time and push next window later — that would raise tail latency. We should check batch_timeout and max_batch_count.

olivia: I profiled a canary earlier. Flamegraph: high time in normalize_attrs() where we allocate and sort attribute keys. Also KV allocations spike.

samir: can you paste the normalized example? are we doing any regex ops or JSON parsing?

olivia: sample from trace (sanitized): {resource: {service.name: "checkout"}, attrs: {user.email_md5: "...", items: [ ... huge array meta ... ]}} — normalization flattens and canonicalizes arrays right now.

maria: here's the relevant config we rolled out (collector):

```yaml
processors:
  attributes_normalizer:
    action: canonicalize
    include: ["attributes.*"]
exporters:
  otlp/custom:
    endpoint: exporters.internal:4317
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, attributes_normalizer]
      exporters: [otlp/custom]
```

josh: that shows normalizer after batch. quick fix options:
- move attributes_normalizer before batch so heavy work is batched and amortized? (but might bloat batch sizes)
- make normalizer cheaper (no array flattening, avoid allocs)
- sample/drop huge attrs earlier (size-based sampling)
- tune batch: reduce batch_timeout_ms to shorten windows or increase exporter threads

vikram: moving it before batch would mean we do normalization once per span then batch the normalized bytes — cheaper overall if normalization is per-span but not per-batch? depends on implementation. If normalization touches many spans it could be duplicated work. We need benchmarks.

maria: I ran a quick AB test on canary: moved normalizer before batch and p99 dropped ~30% but CPU climbed ~12% because allocations moved earlier. When normalizer after batch, CPU lower but exporter latency higher.

samir: tradeoff between CPU and tail latency. For our SLOs we prefer stable p99. Consider hybrid: cheap prefilter to trim large attrs + expensive normalization only for spans that pass size threshold.

olivia: agree. I can add a size_based_filter processor before batch: if span.attributes total_bytes > 2kb then strip keys X,Y,Z and tag sample_reason=truncated. That will reduce worst-case work.

maria: sounds good. Also let's try decreasing batch_timeout_ms from 50 -> 30 in the canary and see how p99 responds. If exporter churn increases, we can raise exporter worker count.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: telemetry-canary/attr-normalizer-fix to 10% at 2026-03-20T15:12:00Z

infra-bot: quick note: watch retention-triggered flushers. If we drop attrs aggressively we'll reduce archived size but metric dashboards for customers might change. Need FH notice.

josh: action items:
- olivia: implement size_based_filter + cheap prefilter (PR by EOD)
- maria: run AB for pre-before-batch vs pre-after-batch with batch_timeout=30 (canary)
- vikram: prepare perf harness & flamegraphs for both configs
- samir: draft FH note about attribute truncation effects

maria: I'll post the canary results in #eng-platform when complete. Thanks all :thumbsup:

olivia: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood/collector/pull/482 — adds size-based drop and moves heavy canonicalize to post-export opt-in.

maria: saw it, kicking the canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary updated: telemetry-canary/attr-normalizer-fix at 20% -> metrics collecting.

josh: monitoring p99 now. preliminary: exporter p99 down 28%, CPU p95 +9%. Logs look cleaner, queue depth stable.

maria: if numbers hold at 20% we'll roll to 100% with a config that uses prefilter + canonicalize behind a feature flag.

samir: fine by me. Will coordinate FH note and keep customers informed. :white_check_mark:

olivia: will follow up with microbench numbers tomorrow.

maria: closing thread for now — reopen if regressions show up.
